title: Project brief, benefits and sustainability management approaches
blurb: Explain the purpose of the project brief and the benefits and sustainability management approaches, and what each adds in an agile project.
question: In an agile project, which management product plans frequent releases so that users and customers start to receive benefits early?

teach.body: Alongside the project canvas, the business case practice in PRINCE2 Agile uses three management products: the project brief, the benefits management approach and the sustainability management approach. Each keeps its PRINCE2 purpose. Table 6.1 of the book explains what each one should add, or stress, when the project is delivered in an agile way.

teach.h: The three products at a glance
head: Product
PRINCE2 purpose
Agile emphasis
rows: A firm foundation for initiating the project
Flexible scope and quality areas; chosen agile techniques; impact on operations
Benefits management actions and benefits reviews
Frequent releases planned for early benefits
Actions, reviews and controls for sustainability targets

teach.caption: Table 6.1; sustainability management approach purpose from PRINCE2 7; Table 3.1 for fix and flex.

teach.body: The project brief still gives the board a firm basis for authorizing initiation. In an agile project it outlines the flexible areas of scope and quality criteria, based on prioritization, and describes the agile techniques and approaches selected, with their expected benefits to the project. Because delivery is incremental, it also gives more detail on how this affects operations and maintenance.

items.label: Board approves brief and release map for initiation
Agree the benefits and sustainability approaches
Check post-project benefit confirmation is planned

teach.h: Benefits on the canvas versus the benefits management approach

rows.label: Answers
values: How will we realize and review them?

steps.label: Measurement and tolerance
steps.sub: how and how far benefits can vary

teach.body: Ashworth Water is rolling out a smart-meter app. Project manager Sunita Rao assembles the project brief: it marks which features and quality criteria can flex, names Scrum with two-week iterations as the chosen approach, and explains how monthly releases will affect the support desk. In initiation the benefits management approach plans a release every month so leak reports start falling early, and the sustainability management approach sets minimum criteria such as low-energy hosting.

teach.text: Do not confuse the sustainability performance target (the project's impact on the wider environment, managed through the sustainability management approach) with agile sustainability (agility that lasts). Also, the benefits management approach PLANS benefits reviews, including after the project; it is not where expected benefits are first listed, which is the canvas.

items: Project brief: firm basis for initiation; in agile it shows flexible scope and quality areas.
It names the agile techniques chosen and their expected benefits, and the impact on operations.
Benefits management approach: benefits actions and reviews; frequent releases for early benefits.
Its content: realization procedures, measurement and tolerance guidance, responsibilities, resources, tools.
Sustainability management approach: actions, reviews and controls for sustainability targets.
Sustainability is fixed for minimum criteria and flexed above them (Table 3.1).

summary: You can now explain the purpose of the project brief and the benefits and sustainability management approaches in an agile project. You can also say what each adds in agile, such as flexible scope areas and frequent releases.

A.q: In an agile project, which product plans frequent releases to enable early delivery of benefits to users or customers?
options: Project brief
Benefits management approach
Commercial management approach
Project canvas
A.why: Table 6.1: in the benefits management approach, frequent releases are planned to enable early delivery of benefits.

whyNot.0: The project brief outlines flexible scope areas and the agile techniques chosen.
whyNot.2: The commercial management approach covers procurement and contracts that support agile working.
whyNot.3: The canvas lists expected benefits; planning their delivery and review is the benefits management approach.

A.q: What should the project brief outline in an agile project?
options: The detailed task list for the first iteration
The final measured benefits of the project
Flexible areas of scope and quality criteria
The skill levels of each team member
A.why: Table 6.1: the brief outlines flexible areas of scope and quality criteria based on prioritization, and the agile techniques chosen.

whyNot.0: Iteration tasks are planned by the team in its team plan.
whyNot.1: Benefits are measured as releases land and after closure, not in the brief.
whyNot.3: Skills are mapped in the team skill matrix.

A.q: What is the purpose of the sustainability management approach?
options: To set actions, reviews and controls for sustainability targets
To make sure agile ways of working continue after the project ends
To record the project's environmental issues as and when they arise
To describe how the team keeps a constant, sustainable working pace
A.why: It defines the actions, reviews and controls needed to achieve the project's sustainability performance targets (PRINCE2 7; agreed in initiation).

whyNot.1: Lasting agility is agile sustainability, a different idea from the sustainability performance target.
whyNot.2: Issues as they arise are recorded through the issues practice (issue register).
whyNot.3: A sustainable working pace is an agile principle, not this approach's purpose.

B.q: Because of incremental delivery, what extra detail should the project brief include?
options: How releases will affect operations and maintenance
A list of every user story in the product backlog
The final budget for each team iteration
The names of the product owners for each team
B.why: Table 6.1: due to incremental delivery, the brief includes more detailed information on how this affects operations and maintenance.

whyNot.1: Detailed user stories sit in product backlogs, not the brief.
whyNot.2: Iteration-level budgets are not a brief requirement; time and cost are fixed per plan level.
whyNot.3: Roles are defined in role descriptions and the team structure (organization practice).

B.q: Which is high-level content of the benefits management approach?
options: User groups and personas for each release
Benefits measurement and tolerance guidance
Agilometer slider ratings for each stage of the project
Story points completed in each iteration
B.why: Table 6.1 lists benefits realization procedures, benefits measurement and tolerance guidance, responsibilities, resources, tools and techniques, standards and references.

whyNot.0: User groups appear on the canvas; personas are a business case technique.
whyNot.2: Agilometer ratings belong to the risk practice.
whyNot.3: Story points per iteration are velocity, a progress measure.

B.q: Under PRINCE2 Agile defaults, how is sustainability treated in fix and flex?
options: Zero tolerance, the same as time and cost
Fixed for Must haves, flexed for Coulds
Fixed for minimum criteria, flexed above
Fully flexed when the budget is tight
B.why: Table 3.1: sustainability is fixed for the minimum criteria and flexed for anything above them.

whyNot.0: Zero tolerance on all levels of plan is the default for time and cost.
whyNot.1: That is the scope row of Table 3.1.
whyNot.3: The minimum criteria stay fixed whatever the budget pressure.

C.q:
Which two statements about these business case products are correct?
1. The project brief describes the agile techniques selected and their expected benefits.
2. The benefits management approach replaces the project canvas.
3. The benefits management approach plans frequent releases for early benefits.
4. The sustainability management approach is created at project closure.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
C.why: Both statements 1 and 3 come from Table 6.1.

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: the canvas is the business case form; the benefits management approach sits alongside it.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: the canvas stays, and the sustainability approach is agreed in initiation.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: the management approaches are agreed in initiating a project.

C.q: A cheaper hosting supplier would let the team add two Could have features but would miss the minimum sustainability criteria. What is the PRINCE2 Agile default view?
options: Accept it, because scope can grow above the minimum
Accept it, because cost has zero tolerance
Reject it, because Could haves are fixed scope
Reject it, because the minimum criteria are fixed
C.why: Sustainability is fixed for minimum criteria (Table 3.1); missing them is not acceptable, however attractive the extra scope.

whyNot.0: Extra scope does not justify breaking the fixed minimum sustainability criteria.
whyNot.1: Cost tolerance is zero, but that does not permit breaking another fixed aspect.
whyNot.2: Could haves are flexible scope; the reason to reject is the sustainability minimum.

C.q: In the 'confirm project acceptance' activity, what is checked about the benefits management approach?
options: That it has been replaced by the end project report
That it includes post-project benefit confirmation
That it lists every user story still in the backlog
That it has been signed off by the team coach
C.why: Confirm project acceptance checks that the benefits management approach includes post-project benefit confirmation (Table 13.18).

whyNot.0: The end project report reviews the project; it does not replace the benefits approach.
whyNot.2: Unfinished work goes into follow-on action recommendations, not the benefits approach.
whyNot.3: The team coach supports delivery teams; the board and business own benefits.

reteach.title: Brief, harvest plan, green rules
reteach.question: Before planting an orchard, what three things would a sensible grower write down?

blocks.body: First a short brief: what we are planting, what can change and how we will work (project brief). Then a harvest plan: when fruit will be picked, how it will be measured and who checks it, with an early crop from fast-growing trees (benefits management approach). Finally green rules that must never drop below a minimum, such as no harmful sprays (sustainability management approach).

blocks.text: The harvest plan (benefits approach) is not the list of fruit you expect (canvas benefits). One says how and when; the other says what.

explain.body: A firm basis for initiation. In agile it outlines flexible areas of scope and quality criteria, the agile techniques chosen and their expected benefits, and the impact on operations and maintenance.

test.q: Which product describes the agile techniques and approaches selected, with their expected benefits to the project?
options: Project brief
Project backlog
Risk register
Team dashboard
test.why: Table 6.1: the project brief includes a description of the agile techniques and approaches selected and their expected benefits.

whyNot.1: The project backlog holds epics and replaces the project product description.
whyNot.3: The team dashboard shows team progress.

explain.body: Defines the benefits management actions and benefits reviews that make sure outcomes are achieved and benefits are confirmed. In agile, frequent releases are planned for early benefits.

options: the roles and responsibilities of the delivery team
the Definition of Done for each team
the tolerances for time and cost on each plan
the benefits actions and benefits reviews
test.why: It defines the benefits management actions and benefits reviews to ensure outcomes are achieved and benefits confirmed.

whyNot.0: Roles and responsibilities are in role descriptions.
whyNot.1: The Definition of Done belongs to quality.
whyNot.2: Time and cost tolerances are set for each plan level, not in this approach.

explain.body: Defines the actions, reviews and controls to achieve the sustainability performance targets. It is agreed in initiation with the other management approaches.

test.q: In which process are the benefits and sustainability management approaches agreed?
options: Starting up a project
Managing product delivery
Closing a project
Initiating a project
test.why: 'Agree the management approaches' in initiating a project covers change, communication, sustainability, benefits, commercial, quality, risk, issue and digital and data (Table 13.6).

whyNot.0: Starting up produces the project brief and the first canvas.
whyNot.1: Managing product delivery is team-level delivery work.
whyNot.2: Closing checks that post-project benefits reviews are planned.

explain.body: Benefits are fixed for minimum viability; sustainability is fixed for minimum criteria. Above those floors, both can flex.

test.q: Which aspect is fixed for minimum criteria and flexed above them?
options: Benefits
Scope
Sustainability
Cost and time
test.why: Sustainability: fixed for minimum criteria, flexed for anything above them (Table 3.1).

whyNot.0: Benefits are fixed for minimum viability, not minimum criteria.
whyNot.1: Scope is fixed for Must haves and flexed for Should and Could haves.
whyNot.3: Time and cost have zero tolerance on all levels of plan.
